sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: Use totem-pole PFC for high-efficiency power factor correction. Replaces the bridge rectifier with active switches for near-zero conduction loss. Requires GaN or SiC MOSFETs for the fast-switching leg (line-frequency commutation).

sections.heading: Controller structure
sections.text: Same voltage/current dual-loop as conventional boost PFC: outer voltage loop (10-20 Hz bandwidth) generates current amplitude reference, inner current loop tracks the sinusoidal reference. The current reference is the voltage-loop output multiplied by the rectified line voltage shape.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: Dead-time management is critical for the fast-switching leg. At light load, ZVS may be lost on the fast-switching leg, causing reverse recovery losses in the body diode. The slow-switching leg operates at line frequency (50/60 Hz) and uses MOSFETs with low Rds_on.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If totem-pole PFC efficiency is below target, check: (1) Is ZVS maintained on the fast-switching leg? (2) Is the dead-time optimized? (3) Are the GaN/SiC devices properly driven? Efficiency loss is usually a hardware issue, not a control issue.
